examinerBank.question: Walk me through your differential diagnosis for this patient and how you would rank it.
examinerBank.modelAnswer: Given a CD4 of 38, disseminated (miliary) TB ranks highest — supported by constitutional symptoms, generalised lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, ascites, a miliary CXR pattern and positive urine LAM/sputum Xpert. Disseminated MAC is a differential at this CD4 threshold but is less common locally and not yet supported by culture. Lymphoma could explain lymphadenopathy and B-symptoms but is refuted by caseating granulomas with AFB on node FNA. Cryptococcal dissemination is considered given the CD4 but the negative serum CrAg and absence of neurological signs argue strongly against it. IRIS is excluded since he has not yet restarted ART.
examinerBank.gradingNotes: Full marks: ranked list with case-specific for/against reasoning tied to CD4 threshold. Partial: unranked or generic list.

examinerBank.question: Why is it critical to establish this patient's CD4 count and ART history early in the consultation, beyond just confirming his HIV status?
examinerBank.modelAnswer: CD4 count is the single most useful discriminator in HIV medicine — it stratifies which opportunistic infections are plausible (e.g. candida <200, CMV/MAC <50) and dictates urgent management decisions such as ART timing relative to TB treatment (within 2 weeks if CD4<50) and need for cotrimoxazole prophylaxis (CD4<200). Nadir CD4 and ART adherence history also explain why an apparently controlled patient has decompensated — in this case, an 8-month treatment default has allowed CD4 to fall from ~250 to 38, permitting disseminated disease.
examinerBank.gradingNotes: Wants explicit CD4-threshold reasoning, not just 'it's important to know his HIV status'.

examinerBank.question: Explain the pathophysiology of the miliary pattern seen on this patient's chest X-ray.
examinerBank.modelAnswer: Miliary TB results from haematogenous dissemination of M. tuberculosis, typically after a caseating focus erodes into a pulmonary vessel (or via lymphohaematogenous spread from a primary complex), showering the bloodstream with bacilli that seed innumerable small granulomas (1-3mm, resembling millet seeds) throughout both lung fields. In profound immunosuppression, CD4 depletion prevents IFN-gamma-mediated macrophage activation, so granulomas cannot organise and contain the infection, permitting widespread dissemination beyond the lungs to liver, spleen, marrow and peritoneum.
examinerBank.gradingNotes: Wants both the vascular erosion mechanism AND the immunological failure of granuloma containment linked to CD4 depletion.

examinerBank.question: His serum cryptococcal antigen test comes back negative. How does this change your interpretation, and would you still consider a lumbar puncture?
examinerBank.modelAnswer: A negative serum CrAg makes disseminated cryptococcal disease very unlikely and does not mandate a diagnostic LP for cryptococcus in an asymptomatic patient (no headache, meningism, or visual change). However, given his CD4<50 and systemic unwellness, TB meningitis remains possible even without overt meningism, so if any neurological symptom develops, an LP with opening pressure and CSF Xpert Ultra should be pursued despite the negative CrAg.
examinerBank.gradingNotes: Tests whether the student understands CrAg's role as a screening step and appropriately reconsiders neuro-invasive TB rather than closing the loop prematurely.

examinerBank.question: Given his CD4 of 38, when would you start ART relative to his TB treatment, and why does this timing matter?
examinerBank.modelAnswer: With CD4<50, ART should be started within 2 weeks of TB treatment initiation, as early ART in profoundly immunosuppressed patients reduces mortality despite a higher risk of TB-IRIS. If CD4 had been ≥50, ART would be deferred to within 8 weeks. The patient and clinical team must be counselled about IRIS — a paradoxical worsening of TB symptoms or new lymphadenopathy in the 2-12 week window after starting ART, caused by immune reconstitution unmasking or exaggerating the inflammatory response to residual mycobacterial antigen.
examinerBank.gradingNotes: Wants the specific CD4-gated timing rule applied correctly, plus recognition of the IRIS trade-off, not just 'start ART soon'.

framework: unwell/deteriorating patient with known or suspected HIV — confirm status, stage disease (CD4/VL/nadir/ART), localise symptoms anatomically, CD4-stratify differential, screen for TB in everyone, consider IRIS timing and drug toxicity, assume dual pathology

patient.name: Sibusiso Mkhize
patient.occupation: security guard, currently not working due to illness
patient.personality: withdrawn, fatigued, gives short answers unless gently encouraged, embarrassed about not taking his treatment properly
patient.openingLine: Doctor... I just feel like I'm wasting away. I don't know what's wrong with me anymore.

presentingComplaint: 3-month history of fever, drenching night sweats and profound weight loss in a patient with known HIV, poorly adherent to ART

history.fact: Symptoms began gradually about 3 months ago with low-grade fevers, now present most days
Fever is present almost daily, worse in the evenings, no clear rigors
Drenching night sweats requiring a change of clothes and bedsheets most nights for the last 6 weeks
Lost approximately 12 kg over 3 months, clothes and belt no longer fit, has noticed his face looking thinner
Has a mild dry cough for about a month, no clear sputum, no haemoptysis
Vague generalised abdominal discomfort and bloating for the past 3-4 weeks, worse after eating
Intermittent loose stools, 2-3 times a day, no blood, no mucus, for about a month
Diagnosed HIV positive 4 years ago; started on TLD but stopped taking it about 8 months ago after moving house and running out of tablets, has not been back to clinic since
Does not know his most recent CD4 count; last one he remembers being told was 'around 250' about a year ago, before he defaulted
No previous TB treatment; his younger brother died of 'chest problems' two years ago, was never properly diagnosed
Has noticed painless lumps in his neck for the past 2 months, slowly growing
No headache, no neck stiffness, no visual disturbance, no confusion reported by himself
No rash, no skin lesions noticed
No other chronic illnesses, no diabetes, no hypertension, never previously hospitalised
Not currently on any medication, stopped cotrimoxazole along with his ART
Lives alone in a backroom in KwaMashu; recently divorced, poor social support; occasional alcohol use, no smoking, no drug use
Has not disclosed his HIV status to anyone, feels ashamed and isolated since his divorce
No urinary symptoms, no joint pains, no chest pain, denies any vomiting or blood in stool

examination.general: Cachectic, chronically ill-looking man. Marked temporal wasting, pallor +, no jaundice, no clubbing. Multiple firm, non-tender, matted lymph nodes palpable in the cervical and axillary chains, largest 2.5cm. Oral thrush present on the palate and buccal mucosa.
examination.respiratory: Trachea central. Reduced air entry at both bases with scattered fine crackles. No overt consolidation or effusion signs. No wheeze.
examination.cardio: Tachycardic, normal heart sounds, no murmurs, JVP not elevated.
examination.abdo: Distended with shifting dullness suggesting mild ascites. Hepatomegaly 4cm below costal margin, tender. Spleen tip palpable. Mild generalised tenderness, no peritonism, no organomegaly-associated masses felt discretely.
examination.neuro: Alert and orientated to person, place and time. No neck stiffness, no photophobia, no focal deficit, no papilloedema on fundoscopy. Peripheral sensation grossly intact.

investigations.name: Sputum GeneXpert MTB/RIF
investigations.result: MTB detected, rifampicin resistance NOT detected

investigations.name: Chest X-ray
investigations.result: Diffuse bilateral micronodular (miliary) pattern with small bilateral pleural effusions

investigations.name: Abdominal ultrasound
investigations.result: Hepatosplenomegaly, multiple hypoechoic para-aortic and mesenteric lymph nodes, mild ascites

investigations.name: Liver function tests
investigations.result: Mild transaminitis: ALT 68, AST 74, ALP 190, albumin 24 g/L (low)

investigations.name: Blood cultures (including mycobacterial blood culture)
investigations.result: Pending — mycobacterial culture sent, results in 2-6 weeks

investigations.name: Ascitic tap (diagnostic)
investigations.result: Exudate, lymphocyte-predominant, ADA elevated at 58 U/L, Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra on fluid: MTB detected

investigations.name: Lymph node fine needle aspirate
investigations.result: Caseating granulomas, AFB seen on ZN stain

for: constitutional symptoms (fever, night sweats, 12kg weight loss)
positive urine TB-LAM and sputum GeneXpert
ascitic fluid ADA elevated with Xpert positive

against: sputum and urine LAM already confirming MTB specifically
MAC less prevalent locally than TB, usually a diagnosis of exclusion here
lymph node FNA shows caseating granulomas with AFB, not malignant cells
no headache, meningism or neurological signs

for: advanced immunosuppression can unmask subclinical infection
against: patient has not restarted ART yet — no recent immune reconstitution to trigger IRIS

pathophys.night sweats and fever: Chronic granulomatous inflammation drives macrophage and T-cell release of TNF-alpha, IL-1 and IL-6, resetting the hypothalamic thermoregulatory set-point; profound immunosuppression allows unchecked mycobacterial proliferation and antigen load, amplifying cytokine release
pathophys.weight loss / cachexia: TNF-alpha (cachectin)-driven catabolism, anorexia from chronic cytokine exposure, and malabsorption from TB-related gut and hepatic involvement, compounded by the direct wasting effect of uncontrolled HIV replication
pathophys.generalised lymphadenopathy: Haematogenous and lymphatic dissemination of M. tuberculosis in the setting of failed granuloma containment (CD4 depletion impairs macrophage activation via IFN-gamma from CD4 T-cells), leading to caseating necrosis within multiple nodal groups
pathophys.hepatosplenomegaly and ascites: Miliary seeding of the reticuloendothelial system (liver, spleen) and peritoneum by haematogenous spread; peritoneal TB produces a lymphocyte-predominant exudative ascites with elevated adenosine deaminase from activated lymphocytes
pathophys.miliary pattern on chest X-ray: Erosion of a caseating focus into a pulmonary vessel (classically after primary infection or reactivation) allows massive haematogenous dissemination of bacilli, seeding innumerable 1-3mm granulomas throughout both lung fields
pathophys.profound CD4 depletion enabling dissemin: Progressive HIV-driven destruction of CD4 T-helper cells impairs IFN-gamma-mediated macrophage activation, the central mechanism that normally walls off M. tuberculosis within organised granulomas; below a CD4 threshold (~50-100) granuloma architecture fails and containment is lost, permitting extrapulmonary and disseminated spread

staging: WHO HIV clinical stage 4 (disseminated/miliary TB); CD4 38 cells/µL (advanced HIV disease); ART-defaulted for 8 months, viral load 680,000 copies/mL

immediate: Admit for further assessment and monitoring given haemodynamic instability (tachycardia, hypotension) and severe wasting
Isolate for airborne precautions pending sputum smear/Xpert result review (respiratory TB component)
Correct hyponatraemia cautiously and provide IV fluids/nutritional support as needed
Screen for other CD4<50 threshold opportunistic disease (fundoscopy for CMV retinitis, serum CrAg — already done, negative)
definitive: Start TB treatment: standard weight-banded 2HRZE/4HR fixed-dose combination (rifampicin-sensitive confirmed)
Start ART (TLD) within 2 weeks of TB treatment initiation given CD4 <50 (early ART in profound immunosuppression reduces mortality despite IRIS risk)
Pyridoxine supplementation with isoniazid to prevent peripheral neuropathy
supportive: Nutritional rehabilitation and dietician referral given BMI 15.8 and severe wasting
Adherence counselling addressing the default — explore barriers (disclosure, social isolation, clinic access)
Psychosocial support and consideration of disclosure counselling given his isolation and stigma concerns
Contact tracing — screen for TB in any household/close contacts
Counsel explicitly on IRIS symptoms/signs before ART initiation given high risk in this CD4 range
followUp: Sputum smear/culture conversion check at 2 months of TB treatment
Repeat CD4 and viral load at 6 months on ART to assess immune recovery and virological suppression
Monitor LFTs given baseline transaminitis, especially once on concurrent TB drugs and ART
Close early follow-up (weeks 2, 4, 8) to detect IRIS, drug toxicity or non-adherence early
Re-engage with adherence support structures/treatment supporter

stationChecklist.item: Introduces self, confirms patient identity, establishes rapport with a withdrawn/ashamed patient, gains consent
stationChecklist.why: Communication skill essential given the patient's stigma and low mood

stationChecklist.item: Confirms HIV status, establishes when diagnosed and WHO stage at diagnosis
stationChecklist.answer: Diagnosed 4 years ago, defaulted ART 8 months ago
stationChecklist.why: Reflex confirmation of HIV status is the first step of the framework in any unexplained illness in KZN

stationChecklist.item: Establishes current/most recent CD4, viral load, nadir CD4, ART regimen and adherence history
stationChecklist.answer: Last known CD4 ~250 a year ago, defaulted TLD 8 months ago, current CD4 will be found to be 38
stationChecklist.why: CD4/VL/nadir/regimen is repeated as the single most useful discriminator in her notes — core organising principle

stationChecklist.item: Screens constitutional symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss) in detail
stationChecklist.answer: Daily evening fevers, drenching night sweats 6 weeks, 12kg weight loss over 3 months

stationChecklist.item: Performs full TB symptom screen (cough, contacts, prior TB treatment) regardless of presenting complaint
stationChecklist.answer: Mild dry cough for a month, brother died of undiagnosed 'chest problems'
stationChecklist.why: "Test/screen everyone" for TB is explicitly emphasised in the framework

stationChecklist.item: Systematically localises symptoms anatomically (GI: abdo pain/diarrhoea; neuro: headache/confusion/vision; lymphatic: lumps) before naming a diagnosis
stationChecklist.answer: Abdominal bloating/diarrhoea present; no headache, neck stiffness or visual symptoms; painless enlarging neck lumps
stationChecklist.why: Symptom-to-differential reasoning requires anatomical localisation before diagnosis

stationChecklist.item: Explores adherence barriers, disclosure status and social support sensitively
stationChecklist.answer: Non-disclosed, isolated after divorce, ran out of tablets and never returned to clinic
stationChecklist.why: Adherence barriers are key to both diagnosis (advanced disease) and future management planning

stationChecklist.item: Performs general examination noting wasting, pallor, lymphadenopathy, oral thrush, skin
stationChecklist.answer: Cachectic, temporal wasting, matted cervical/axillary nodes, oral thrush
stationChecklist.why: General signs stage the severity of immunosuppression and guide differential

stationChecklist.item: Performs focused respiratory, abdominal and neurological examination
stationChecklist.answer: Reduced air entry with crackles, hepatosplenomegaly with ascites (shifting dullness), no meningism/focal neurology
stationChecklist.why: Localises disseminated pathology across systems as per framework step 3

stationChecklist.item: Offers ranked, CD4-stratified differential with reasoning (disseminated TB > MAC > lymphoma > cryptococcal disease > IRIS)
stationChecklist.why: CD4-stratified differential reasoning is the exam philosophy explicitly taught in her notes

stationChecklist.item: Requests CD4, viral load, sputum GeneXpert, urine TB-LAM, CXR, serum CrAg, abdominal ultrasound, and considers ascitic tap/lymph node FNA for tissue diagnosis
stationChecklist.answer: See investigations catalogue — confirms disseminated TB with negative CrAg excluding concurrent cryptococcal disease
stationChecklist.why: Confirmatory pathway per SA TB/HIV guidelines; CrAg specifically screens for a key CD4<100 differential

stationChecklist.item: Outlines TB treatment (2HRZE/4HR), correct ART timing given CD4<50 (within 2 weeks), cotrimoxazole restart, pyridoxine, notification, contact tracing, and explicit IRIS counselling
stationChecklist.why: CD4-specific ART timing and IRIS anticipation are management anchors central to this framework
